inputs.wacc_rationale: 10.0% in CNY/HKD terms: China 10y CGB ~1.8-2.0% + ~7% China equity risk premium at beta ~1.1 + small-cap/governance adjustment ~0.5pp. Applied identically to all three scenarios; Letybo-licence, VBP and receivables-conversion risk are carried in the bear flows and the 30% bear weight, not stacked on the discount rate.

inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once. (1) Xuanzhu Biopharm (2575.HK) is still a consolidated subsidiary after its Oct-2025 IPO (non-wholly-owned, 49.13% effective at FY2025 note 18; group holds 254,859,125 H shares = 49.21% per the H1-2026 directors'-interests table) with ~51% NCI. It is REMOVED from the flows (revenue, losses, capex) and from cash, and the group's stake enters the bridge at market less 20%. (2) Huisheng Biopharm investors' stakes sit as redemption liabilities (RMB1,347.0m, note 15(iv)) deducted as debt-like in the bridge; no further leakage charged for them. (3) Medical-aesthetics NCI (Meiyan Space now 90% after the H1-2026 step-up from 77%) folded into the cash-tax/leakage driver as ~4-6pp on top of tax.
inputs.interest_treatment: Interest received is classified in INVESTING and interest paid in FINANCING on Sihuan's cash-flow statement, so reported FCF (OCF - PP&E - intangibles) already excludes interest income; the interest_income deduction is 0 to avoid stripping it twice. The cash pile enters once, in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route) on the ex-Xuanzhu operating group (medical aesthetics + generics + Huisheng/other medicines + HQ), PLUS a sum-of-parts bridge: listed Xuanzhu stake at market less 20%, Xuanzhu's own cash removed, equity-method associates and unlisted equity investments at book, redemption liabilities and other borrowings deducted. Chosen because it is an operating pharma/aesthetics company (routing table row 2: non-US operating company + NCI/non-operating-asset adaptations); the only distortion large enough to need a separate part is Xuanzhu, which is listed, loss-making and ~51% owned by others, so its value is observable and its losses would otherwise contaminate the margin build. FY0 BASE: FY2025 revenue RMB2,618.0m less Xuanzhu standalone revenue RMB51.8m (2575.HK FY2025, Yahoo fundamentals) = 2,566.2. reported_fcf (ex-Xuanzhu) = consolidated -218.1 (OCF -23.6, PP&E -58.3, intangibles -136.2) plus Xuanzhu FY2025 FCF burn 252.5 added back = 34.4; last_fcf = 34.4 - 9.0 SBC = 25.4. FY2025 consolidated OCF was crushed by a RMB690.8m receivables build (revenue +717m) and H1-2026 OCF was -92m with receivables up another ~RMB432m on flat revenue; the FY2026-27 margin path is set below the H1-2026 run-rate to allow for that conversion drag, and the H1-2026 cash burn is already in the 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet. ONE-OFFS EXCLUDED: FY2019 ~RMB4.0bn impairment (Key Monitoring Drug List), FY2022 ~RMB1.7bn VBP impairment, FY2024 RMB418m Xuanzhu share-based payment, H1-2026 RMB154.2m gain on disposal of a subsidiary and RMB110.7m associate investee gain / RMB64.2m associate impairment. BUYBACKS: the company is an active repurchaser (RMB188.6m FY2025, RMB41.9m H1-2026), so the flat count is funded, not a convention. FY0 calibration: FY2026E NOPAT ~RMB260m vs FY2025 attributable NI 179.7 which carried ~49% of Xuanzhu's -245.5m loss (~-120m) and ~RMB150m+ of redemption-liability interest; ex-Xuanzhu attributable ~RMB300m, tie within non-operating noise.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (-8.6%) is distorted by the FY2019/FY2022 impairments and RMB1.3-1.4bn special dividends; EPS 3yr undefined (FY2022 loss); owner-FCF CAGRs undefined (FY2022-FY2025 reported FCF negative, -547/-96/+58/-218). Revenue 3yr used as the only clean series, and it mixes a doubling aesthetics business with a halving generics business.
historical_growth.notes: SBC is negligible outside the FY2024 one-off, so SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs do not diverge for SBC reasons; the divergence that matters is working capital (receivables) and Xuanzhu's burn.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026: aesthetics ~+17% (H1 +18.5%) to ~RMB1.74bn, Huisheng/other ~RMB0.4bn, generics roughly halved to ~RMB0.4bn by VBP and divestments -> ~flat. FY2027-29: generics stabilise at a small base, aesthetics +12-15%, Huisheng semaglutide/insulin launches; fades to 3% by FY2035.
base.ebitda_rationale: H1-2026 ex-Xuanzhu ex-gains EBITDA ~29% of revenue; FY2026 set at 26% for receivable impairment/conversion drag and the generics loss (-RMB74m H1), rising to 31% as generics shrinks and aesthetics (segment margin ~50%) becomes ~70% of revenue. Letybo is licensed from Hugel, so the margin is capped below an IP owner's.
base.tax_rationale: PRC 25% statutory, unshielded generics losses in separate entities, dividend WHT on upstreaming, plus ~10% aesthetics NCI leakage on post-tax profit. H1-2026 group effective rate ~42% (FY2025 ~56%) is inflated by Xuanzhu losses; ramps to 32%.
base.wc_rationale: Negative: receivables + inventory are ~110% of revenue (RMB2.37bn + 0.56bn vs ~RMB2.6bn); FY2025 consumed RMB579m of working capital on +RMB717m revenue.

scenario_narratives.base: Medical aesthetics keeps compounding at mid-teens near term as Letybo holds ~22-25% toxin share and the self-developed PLLA/PCL fillers and collagen products add a second leg; the Hugel licence is renewed past 2030 on similar economics. Generics roughly halves again in FY2026 under VBP and divestments and then stabilises as a small, near-breakeven cash ballast. Huisheng's insulin and semaglutide launches add growth from FY2027. Receivables stop outgrowing revenue but working capital still absorbs ~40% of incremental revenue. Xuanzhu is worth its discounted market price, no more.
scenario_narratives.bull: Aesthetics beats the >30% key-product share target by 2027, the Meiyan Space buyout to 100% removes the remaining leakage, Huisheng's semaglutide becomes a meaningful obesity/diabetes product, and the generics drag disappears quickly through disposals. Margin reaches 34% as aesthetics passes ~75% of revenue, and Xuanzhu's market value recovers toward its IPO-plus range (upside to the bridge not modelled).
scenario_narratives.bear: Domestic toxin competition (new approvals, Imeik/Bloomage/Haohai fillers) and weaker discretionary spending compress Letybo pricing; the Hugel licence that runs to end-2030 is renewed on materially worse terms or lost, taking ~12% of revenue out in FY2031. VBP cuts reach the remaining generics faster than they can be sold, and receivables owed by aesthetics chains prove partly uncollectable (FY2025 already booked RMB52m of receivable impairment). Margin compresses to 18%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 30%: the thesis rests on an unproven pivot whose largest product is licensed, not owned (Hugel, to 2030), and two years of profit have not converted to operating cash (receivables +RMB1.1bn in 18 months). Base 50%: H1-2026 aesthetics growth and the swing to profit are real. Bull 20%: needs Huisheng's GLP-1, the aesthetics share target and a clean generics exit all to go right together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the business Sihuan's shareholders actually own: the aesthetics-led operating group on an owner-FCF basis, plus its listed 49% of Xuanzhu at a discount to market, plus net cash after the redemption liabilities owed to Huisheng's investors. Exclude every one-off (impairments, the 2024 Xuanzhu SBC charge, 2026 disposal gains) from the margin base, and make working capital pay for growth because this company's receivables have been growing faster than its revenue.
key_risks_to_valuation: Letybo is licensed from Hugel to end-2030; non-renewal or worse terms is the single largest value driver and is the bear case
Receivables quality: trade and other receivables rose from RMB1.94bn to RMB2.37bn in H1-2026 on flat revenue; operating cash flow was negative in FY2025 and H1-2026
Xuanzhu stake (~RMB1.46bn after discount, ~RMB0.16/share) is marked to a volatile market price that is ~90% off its peak
Redemption liabilities (RMB1.35bn, current) could be called in cash if Huisheng's contingent events occur
Net cash is large relative to market cap; its value to minorities depends on capital allocation (buybacks continuing vs. aesthetics M&A and the Meiyan NCI buyout)
